column1: # procedure-layers.tsv — the specification layers getProcedureFlow retrieves from.
# A 3GPP procedure is never in one spec: the flow is in a stage-2 architecture
# spec, the messages in a stage-3 signalling spec, the radio legs elsewhere. This
# table declares which layers exist, in what order, and which spec families each
# generation prefers. It replaces a hard-coded list in ThreeGppToolService.
# Two row types, tab-separated, first column names the type.
#   layer <TAB> series <TAB> order <TAB> technology <TAB> perLayer <TAB> prefer <TAB> label
#   series      3GPP series number to scope the retrieval to
#   order       ascending display order; also the natural reading order of a flow
#   technology  5G | LTE | ANY — which requests this row applies to.
#               A request for technology=5G runs rows marked 5G and ANY.
#   perLayer    max chunks from this layer before the evidence floor is applied
#   prefer      comma-separated spec-id prefixes boosted WITHIN this layer, or "-"
#   label       human heading printed above the layer's evidence
# `technology` used to gate only the radio layer, so an LTE question still had
# 23.502 (5G procedures) competing against 23.401 (EPS procedures) in the core
# layer. Measured: "EPS attach" scoped to series 23 returned 23.502 at 0.768 and
# pushed 23.401 down to rank 4 (0.648). `prefer` is a ranking boost, NOT a hard
# filter — cross-generation evidence still surfaces when genuinely relevant,
# which matters for interworking procedures like SRVCC and EPS fallback.
# ── technology aliases: how callers spell a generation → canonical value ─────
